Ui.Script:
-- NUM_BAG_SLOTS is this file's in the reference too (BankFrame.lua:2), and it is read from -- outside it: the sourced `ContainerFrame.lua` (1751) branches on it in -- `ContainerFrame_OnShow` to tell an equipped bag from a bank bag, and `updateContainer -- FrameAnchors` measures against `BankFrame`. Lua resolves at CALL time, so this file -- sitting far below ContainerFrame.xml in the manifest is fine — but the ownership is the -- reference's, not a convenience. NUM_BAG_SLOTS = 4 -- (ref BankFrame.lua:2) NUM_BANKGENERIC_SLOTS = 24 -- (ref BankFrame.lua:3) NUM_BANKBAGSLOTS = 6 -- (ref BankFrame.lua:4)
-- ══ THE CONTAINER-SLOT KIT — moved here from BagFrame.xml with decision 1751's bag swap ══ -- -- `BenillaBagSlotTemplate` and the `BenillaBagSlot_*` bodies below were the bag WINDOWS' -- slot machinery, and this window borrowed them for its 24 vault slots. The bag windows are -- now the reference's own `ContainerFrame1..12`, executed off the player's chain (1751), and -- their slots are the reference's `ContainerFrameItemButtonTemplate`. That leaves this -- window as the kit's ONLY consumer, so the kit lives here — where the next migration -- (BankFrame's own stock files, whose `BankItemButtonTemplate`/`BankFrameItemButton_*` -- replace all of it) deletes it in one piece. -- -- Names unchanged on purpose: 144 `inherits=` sites and ~145 `<OnLoad>` calls in this file -- write them, and a rename would be churn on code whose whole future is deletion. -- -- Fully generic over `button:GetParent():GetID()`, which is why the move is a move and not -- a rewrite — this window carries `id="-1"` (BANK_CONTAINER) and its buttons resolve their -- container from it exactly as a bag window's did from theirs.
-- BenillaBagSlot_OnLoad(button, physIndex): physIndex is the button's CHAIN position (1 = -- bottom-right, growing up-and-left — the anchor order below), not the game slot. The ref's -- own formula (index = size - j + 1, ContainerFrame.lua:426/446) maps chain position → game -- slot dynamically in BenillaBagSlot_Update, so slot 1 always reads top-left regardless of -- how many of the window's slots are actually occupied — recomputed every Update (the ref -- only computes it once, at window generation; recomputing is a strict robustness win for -- the rare live bag-swap case, not a behavior change for a size that never moves). function BenillaBagSlot_OnLoad(button, physIndex) button.physIndex = physIndex button.icon = getglobal(button:GetName() .. "Icon") button.count = getglobal(button:GetName() .. "Count") -- Both buttons must reach OnClick (the default set is LeftButtonUp only): LEFT-click is the -- pickup gesture (PickupContainerItem — pick up / place / swap on the cursor); RIGHT-click -- cancels a held cursor, else uses the slot (the C side sells it when a merchant is open — -- our container drain forks). button:RegisterForClicks("LeftButtonUp", "RightButtonUp") -- The drag trio (decision 0216 §3): click-carry and drag are ONE code path in the -- reference (ContainerFrame.xml:40-55 routes OnDragStart/OnReceiveDrag to the same -- OnClick("LeftButton", ignoreModifiers=1) the plain click uses) — see -- BenillaBagSlot_OnClick below for the identical routing (its own `ignoreModifiers` -- suppresses the shift-split fork, the reference's own contract for drag/receive). button:RegisterForDrag("LeftButton") BenillaBagSlot_Update(button) end
function BenillaBagSlot_OnClick(button, mouseButton, ignoreModifiers) if button.slot == nil then return end -- a hidden button (physIndex past the bag's size) local bagId = button:GetParent():GetID() if mouseButton == "LeftButton" then -- The reference's own five returns (ContainerFrame.lua:241) — decision 1199 -- put this binding back on its 1.12 shape. local texture, itemCount, locked, quality, readable = GetContainerItemInfo(bagId, button.slot) -- The modifier fork, the reference's own order (ContainerFrame.lua:563-579; -- BankFrame.lua:141-152 for a bank slot, which is this same handler at container -- -1). `ignoreModifiers` (the drag-trio calls, both true) suppresses it whole — -- the reference's drag/receive contract. -- -- CTRL: preview the item on your own character in the dressing room (decision 1060). if IsControlKeyDown() and not ignoreModifiers then DressUpItemLink(GetContainerItemLink(bagId, button.slot)) return end -- SHIFT: post the item's link into the chat edit box if it's open, ELSE split the -- stack. The ref's own `else` (l.567-577) — and note it gates on `IsShown()` here -- where its siblings use `IsVisible()`; ours are the same thing (the edit box's only -- parent is UIParent), so the ref's own word is quoted at each site. if IsShiftKeyDown() and not ignoreModifiers then -- The visibility test is the REF'S fork, not the helper's: with chat open this -- arm never splits, even in the one benilla state where nothing can be posted -- (an unresolved template — `BenillaChatEdit_InsertLink`'s own note). if ChatFrameEditBox and ChatFrameEditBox:IsShown() then BenillaChatEdit_InsertLink(GetContainerItemLink(bagId, button.slot)) return end if texture ~= nil and not locked and (itemCount or 1) >= 2 then button.SplitStack = function(btn, n) SplitContainerItem(bagId, btn.slot, n) BenillaBankFrame_RepaintItems() end -- Ref ContainerFrameItemButton_OnLoad/_OnClick (ContainerFrame.lua:558-560, -- 573-576): the owner's own SplitStack closure carries the bag/slot so -- StackSplitFrameOkay_Click's generic `owner.SplitStack(owner, split)` call -- needs no window-specific knowledge. SplitContainerItem lives in cursor.rs -- rather than container.rs — it is the one container-named verb whose -- payload is the cursor's, not a bag's — but like every container verb it is -- a plain top-level global (decision 1198). OpenStackSplitFrame(itemCount, button, "BOTTOMRIGHT", "TOPRIGHT") end return end -- A plain click hides any open split frame (ref ContainerFrame.lua:581) before the -- ordinary pickup/place proceeds. local split = getglobal("StackSplitFrame") if split then split:Hide() end -- PickupContainerItem is the single drag entry point (real client): an empty cursor -- picks this slot up; a held cursor places/swaps into it (same slot = cancel). Hide the -- hover tooltip (the item just left the slot for the cursor) and repaint so the picked -- slot dims / un-dims immediately — the swap itself settles when the server answers. PickupContainerItem(bagId, button.slot) GameTooltip:Hide() BenillaBankFrame_RepaintItems() elseif mouseButton == "RightButton" then -- A held cursor cancels (client-side, nothing sent); otherwise use/equip/sell the slot. if CursorHasItem() then ClearCursor() BenillaBankFrame_RepaintItems() else UseContainerItem(bagId, button.slot) end end end
-- Hover: the era-true GameTooltip:SetBagItem(bag, slot) — the ENGINE renders the full -- item tooltip from the template store and owns the sell-price money law (real instance -- + merchant open + repair off ⇒ OnTooltipAddMoney(SellPrice × stack), or the -- ITEM_UNSELLABLE line — wow-re ui/scratch/tooltip-money.md's byte-verified gate, -- decision 0274 P1). The durability-adjusted damaged price is deferred until durability -- damage reaches the feed (a pristine item reduces to SellPrice × stack, the case we -- ship). Nothing shows while the template is in flight — the OnUpdate re-enter fills it. function BenillaBagSlot_OnEnter(button) if button.slot == nil then return end local bagId = button:GetParent():GetID() local texture, itemCount, locked, quality, readable = GetContainerItemInfo(bagId, button.slot) -- An emptied slot drops its tooltip (ref ContainerFrame_Update's texture-nil branch, -- ContainerFrame.lua:281-283) — without this the OnUpdate re-enter below would leave -- a stale tooltip up after the item is sold or moved out from under the hover. if not texture then if GameTooltip:IsOwned(button) then GameTooltip:Hide() end return end -- Ref ContainerFrameItemButton_OnEnter (ContainerFrame.lua:602-612) verbatim: a slot -- in the RIGHT half of the screen hangs its tooltip LEFT, so it never runs off the -- edge (the bag lives at the bottom-right — this is the ref's own screen-edge answer, -- a side-pick, not a clamp). if (button:GetRight() or 0) >= (GetScreenWidth() / 2) then GameTooltip:SetOwner(button, "ANCHOR_LEFT") else GameTooltip:SetOwner(button, "ANCHOR_RIGHT") end GameTooltip:SetBagItem(bagId, button.slot) -- The pouch/magnifier cursor (ref ContainerFrameItemButton_OnEnter tail, -- ContainerFrame.lua l.636-642): merchant open on the MERCHANT tab and not repair -- mode → the sell cursor over this slot; else a readable item (a mail letter copy — -- right-click opens the reader) → the Inspect magnifier; anything else restores the -- base cursor. The OnUpdate re-enter keeps it current while hovering (the ref's own -- loop). The ref's `IsControlKeyDown() and hasItem` magnifier arm (l.638) is the -- dress-up preview's own cursor tell — it landed with the dressing room (decision -- 1060); `info` is non-nil above, which is the ref's `hasItem`. if MerchantFrame and MerchantFrame:IsShown() and MerchantFrame.selectedTab == 1 and not InRepairMode() then ShowContainerSellCursor(bagId, button.slot) elseif readable or IsControlKeyDown() then ShowInspectCursor() else ResetCursor() end GameTooltip:Show() end
function BenillaBagSlot_OnLeave(button) GameTooltip:Hide() -- Ref ItemButton OnLeave (ContainerFrame.xml): the hover's sell cursor drops with it. ResetCursor() end
-- Ref ContainerFrameItemButton_OnUpdate (ContainerFrame.lua:645-660): while the tooltip -- is ours, re-run OnEnter every frame — the ref ships this loop UNTHROTTLED (its -- updateTooltip throttle is commented out in 1.12). It is the real client's own refresh -- mechanism: a tooltip set while the item template was still in flight fills itself in -- the moment the answer lands, no re-hover. function BenillaBagSlot_OnUpdate(button) if GameTooltip:IsOwned(button) then BenillaBagSlot_OnEnter(button) end end
-- The item's use-cooldown sweep (ref ContainerFrame_UpdateCooldown, -- ContainerFrame.lua:295-299, verbatim shape over our container dialect). function BenillaBagSlot_UpdateCooldown(button, bagId) local cooldown = getglobal(button:GetName() .. "Cooldown") local start, duration, enable = GetContainerItemCooldown(bagId, button.slot) CooldownFrame_SetTimer(cooldown, start, duration, enable) end
-- The physIndex → game-slot resolution (the module doc above) + the paint (ref -- ContainerFrame_Update, ContainerFrame.lua:234-293). Shared by every window's slot -- buttons. The occupied/empty fork drives the cooldown exactly as the ref does -- (l.248-253: occupied → UpdateCooldown, empty → Cooldown:Hide()). function BenillaBagSlot_Update(button) local bagId = button:GetParent():GetID() local size = GetContainerNumSlots(bagId) if button.physIndex > size then button.slot = nil button:Hide() return end button.slot = size - button.physIndex + 1 button:Show() local texture, itemCount, locked = GetContainerItemInfo(bagId, button.slot) if texture ~= nil or itemCount ~= nil then BenillaBagSlot_UpdateCooldown(button, bagId) button.icon:SetTexture(texture or BENILLA_FALLBACK_ICON) -- A locked slot (its item is up on the cursor, or a send is still pending -- server-side, decision 0216 §4/0218 §3) dims, the real client's drag feedback. if locked then button.icon:SetVertexColor(0.4, 0.4, 0.4) else button.icon:SetVertexColor(1, 1, 1) end if (itemCount or 1) > 1 then button.count:SetText(itemCount) else button.count:SetText("") end else button.icon:SetTexture(nil) button.count:SetText("") getglobal(button:GetName() .. "Cooldown"):Hide() end end function BankFrame_OnLoad() local frame = this -- Named directly rather than through `$parent .. "Portrait"`: the reference's bank -- portrait is the UNPREFIXED global `BankPortraitTexture` (ref BankFrame.xml l.93), -- one of the reference's own naming inconsistencies, and it is the name addons write. -- `Bagnon_Core/Events.lua:41` does `SetPortraitTexture(BankPortraitTexture, "npc")` -- when its "show Bagnon's bank instead" option is off, and against a nil first argument -- that binding raises. Same standing lesson as `ToggleBackpack` / `CharacterBag0Slot`: -- the name an addon reaches for is the reference's, not ours. SetPortraitTexture(BankPortraitTexture, "npc") frame:RegisterEvent("BANKFRAME_OPENED") frame:RegisterEvent("BANKFRAME_CLOSED") frame:RegisterEvent("PLAYERBANKSLOTS_CHANGED") frame:RegisterEvent("PLAYERBANKBAGSLOTS_CHANGED") frame:RegisterEvent("PLAYER_MONEY") -- Container -1 is a container like any other: the same lock/cooldown maintenance -- events a bag window registers (the reference's `ContainerFrame_OnLoad`), handled -- below by BankFrame_OnEvent directly: this window's 24 slots are its own, painted by -- BenillaBankFrame_RepaintItems over the slot kit above. frame:RegisterEvent("ITEM_LOCK_CHANGED") frame:RegisterEvent("BAG_UPDATE_COOLDOWN") end
-- The banker's name arrives as arg1 of BANKFRAME_OPENED (the app resolves the banker guid -- through the NameCache — the merchant/trainer feed's own ask-once pattern); nil/empty -- until it lands, or if this ever fires with no name, falls back to "Banker". function BenillaBankFrame_SetTitle(name) if name == nil or name == "" then name = "Banker" end getglobal("BankFrameTitleText"):SetText(name) end
-- Repaint every one of the 24 generic slots (PLAYERBANKSLOTS_CHANGED names ONE slot; the -- spec allows repainting all 24 — cheap, and spares tracking a slot->button map). function BenillaBankFrame_RepaintItems() for i = 1, NUM_BANKGENERIC_SLOTS do local button = getglobal("BankItem" .. i) if button then BenillaBagSlot_Update(button) end end end
-- The bag row (ref UpdateBagSlotStatus, BankFrame.lua:81-117): each button's icon from the -- app-resolved BenillaGetBankBagTexture feed (falling back to the empty paper-doll bag -- slot art), tinted white when purchased / red when not; the purchase row's cost coins + -- afford color; the whole row hidden once GetNumBankSlots() reports `full`. function BenillaBankFrame_UpdateBagRow() local numSlots, full = GetNumBankSlots() for i = 1, NUM_BANKBAGSLOTS do local button = getglobal("BankBagButton" .. i) if button then local texture = BenillaGetBankBagTexture(i) button.icon:SetTexture(texture or "Interface\\PaperDoll\\UI-PaperDoll-Slot-Bag") if i <= numSlots then button.icon:SetVertexColor(1.0, 1.0, 1.0) button.tooltipText = "Bag Slot" -- BANK_BAG else button.icon:SetVertexColor(1.0, 0.1, 0.1) button.tooltipText = "Purchasable Bag Slot" -- BANK_BAG_PURCHASE end end end
local cost = GetBankSlotCost(numSlots) BankFrame.nextSlotCost = cost BenillaMoney_Set("BankFrameCostMoney", cost, true) if GetMoney() >= cost then BenillaMoney_SetColor("BankFrameCostMoney", 1.0, 1.0, 1.0) else BenillaMoney_SetColor("BankFrameCostMoney", 1.0, 0.1, 0.1) end
local purchaseFrame = getglobal("BankFramePurchaseInfo") if full then purchaseFrame:Hide() else purchaseFrame:Show() end end
-- `UpdateBagSlotStatus()` — THE REFERENCE'S NAME for the pass above, published for the same -- standing reason `ToggleBackpack` and `BagSlotButton_OnEnter` are: an addon calls the -- client's global, and it must exist and do the job. `Bagnon_Core/Events.lua:46` calls it -- from its own `ShowBlizBank()`, two lines after `SetPortraitTexture(BankPortraitTexture, …)` -- above — the path taken whenever a player turns Bagnon's "show Bagnon at the bank" option -- OFF and gets the stock window instead. It was nil, so that whole handler died there. -- -- The reference's own body walks its `BankFrameBag1..6` and repaints -- `BankFrameDetailMoneyFrame`; ours is the same pass over our own bag row and cost frame, -- which is exactly what the reference's does for its window (it is not a shim: it is this -- window's real update, under the name the client publishes it as). function UpdateBagSlotStatus() BenillaBankFrame_UpdateBagRow() end
function BankFrame_OnEvent(event) local frame = this if event == "BANKFRAME_OPENED" then BenillaBankFrame_SetTitle(arg1) BenillaBankFrame_RepaintItems() BenillaBankFrame_UpdateBagRow() ShowUIPanel(frame) elseif event == "BANKFRAME_CLOSED" then HideUIPanel(frame) elseif event == "PLAYERBANKSLOTS_CHANGED" then BenillaBankFrame_RepaintItems() elseif event == "PLAYERBANKBAGSLOTS_CHANGED" then BenillaBankFrame_UpdateBagRow() elseif event == "PLAYER_MONEY" then BenillaMoney_Set("BankFrameMoney", GetMoney()) BenillaBankFrame_UpdateBagRow() -- the cost coins' afford color can flip too elseif event == "ITEM_LOCK_CHANGED" then if arg1 == -1 then BenillaBankFrame_RepaintItems() end elseif event == "BAG_UPDATE_COOLDOWN" then -- No bag argument (ref l.243-253's own shape) — BenillaBagSlot_Update's occupied -- leg re-runs the cooldown sweep as part of the full 24-slot repaint. BenillaBankFrame_RepaintItems() end end
function BenillaBankFrame_CloseButton_OnClick() CloseBankFrame() HideUIPanel(getglobal("BankFrame")) end
-- CloseBankBagFrames (ref BankFrame.lua:119-123) — now VERBATIM, because the bank bags are -- ordinary ContainerFrames again (1751): ids NUM_BAG_SLOTS+1 .. +NUM_BANKBAGSLOTS, closed -- through the reference's own `CloseBag`. The button's lit ring follows from -- `ContainerFrame_OnHide`, which calls `UpdateBagButtonHighlight` for every id above -- NUM_BAG_SLOTS — so this no longer unchecks the buttons itself. function CloseBankBagFrames() for i = NUM_BAG_SLOTS + 1, NUM_BAG_SLOTS + NUM_BANKBAGSLOTS do CloseBag(i) end end
-- UpdateBagButtonHighlight(id) — ref BankFrame.lua:171-185, and the reference's own callers -- are the sourced `ContainerFrame_OnShow`/`_OnHide`: every container id above NUM_BAG_SLOTS -- routes its lit-state here instead of to a `CharacterBag<N>Slot`. Without it, opening a -- bank bag raises inside the reference's file. -- -- ONE DIVERGENCE, in the art and not the rule: the reference lights a dedicated -- `BankFrameBag<n>HighlightFrameTexture` that its bag button carries; ours is a CheckButton -- whose CheckedTexture is that highlight (this file's own lit-ring convention, shared with -- the equipped-bag bar). So the same question — "is this bag's window open?" — writes -- `SetChecked` rather than showing a texture, and `IsBagOpen` asks it instead of the -- reference's open-coded ContainerFrame scan, which is the same scan under a name the -- reference itself publishes. function UpdateBagButtonHighlight(id) local button = getglobal("BankBagButton" .. (id - NUM_BAG_SLOTS)) if not button then return end button:SetChecked(IsBagOpen(id) and 1 or nil) end
-- ── The 6 bag buttons (ref BankFrameItemButtonBag_OnClick/_OnShiftClick, BankFrame.lua: -- 171-204): NOT container slots (they hold a whole BAG item, not a stack) — the doll -- pickup idiom BagFrame.xml's BenillaBagBarSlot_* already established for the equipped -- bag slots, reused verbatim here over BankButtonIDToInvSlotID's bag arm (id 1..6 -> -- live 64..69). A held cursor item always PLACES; an empty cursor toggles the button's -- popout window instead (ref: PutItemInBag first, ToggleBag only if that failed). ── function BenillaBankBagButton_OnLoad(button, id) button:SetID(id) button.icon = getglobal(button:GetName() .. "Icon") -- Both buttons, ref-verbatim (BankItemButtonBagTemplate's OnLoad runs -- BankFrameBagButton_OnLoad -> BankFrameBaseButton_OnLoad, BankFrame.lua:12); the vault -- slots get the same pair through BenillaBagSlot_OnLoad. The OnClick below reads no -- button — right-click places/opens exactly as left does. button:RegisterForClicks("LeftButtonUp", "RightButtonUp") button:RegisterForDrag("LeftButton") end
function BenillaBankBagButton_Place(button) PickupInventoryItem(BankButtonIDToInvSlotID(button:GetID(), 1)) PlaySound("BAGMENUBUTTONPRESS") end
function BenillaBankBagButton_OnClick(button) if CursorHasItem() then BenillaBankBagButton_Place(button) return end -- A bank bag's window is a ContainerFrame like any other now (1751), at container id -- NUM_BAG_SLOTS + <slot> — the reference's own arrangement, and the one decision 0604 -- quoted ("the reference reuses ContainerFrames for bank bags identically") before this -- engine had `ToggleBag` to reuse them with. So the whole popout fork below is the -- reference's single call, and `ToggleBag`'s own `size > 0` guard is the "only a slot -- holding a bag opens" rule this file used to spell out. local id = NUM_BAG_SLOTS + button:GetID() PlaySound("BAGMENUBUTTONPRESS") ToggleBag(id) -- The lit ring: `ContainerFrame_OnShow`/`_OnHide` route here for a bank id, so this -- tail is the ref's own (BankFrameItemButtonBag_OnClick l.195) and covers the case -- ToggleBag declined — a bagless or unpurchased slot leaves the button unlit. UpdateBagButtonHighlight(id) end
function BenillaBankBagButton_OnEnter(button) GameTooltip:SetOwner(button, "ANCHOR_RIGHT") GameTooltip:SetText(button.tooltipText or "Bag Slot") GameTooltip:Show() end
-- The Purchase button (ref BankFramePurchaseButton OnClick, BankFrame.xml:478-482) + its -- confirm popup (ref StaticPopup.lua CONFIRM_BUY_BANK_SLOT, l.47-58 — text-only here, see -- the header's money-frame note). Accept queues PurchaseSlot(); the descriptor's byte-2 -- delta is the only success signal (decision 0604) — PLAYERBANKBAGSLOTS_CHANGED repaints. function BenillaBankFramePurchaseButton_OnClick() PlaySound("igMainMenuOption") StaticPopup_Show("CONFIRM_BUY_BANK_SLOT") end
StaticPopupDialogs["CONFIRM_BUY_BANK_SLOT"] = { text = "Do you want to purchase a bank slot for:", -- CONFIRM_BUY_BANK_SLOT button1 = "Yes", button2 = "No", OnAccept = function() PurchaseSlot() end, timeout = 0, hideOnEscape = 1, }

FontString.text: Do you wish to purchase space for an additional bag?
